title: Elton John urges Australia to protect artists from AI at the Aria awards
excerpt: Elton John used an Aria awards message to urge Australia not to let AI firms use artists' work without permission, backing Not AI's To Take.
content_html:
Elton John used a pre-recorded message at the Aria awards in Sydney on Wednesday to urge the Australian government to protect artists from AI firms, the Guardian reported. He backed Not AI’s To Take, a new campaign by the creative and media industries.

“You have a duty to protect Australian artists and their work. Don’t let AI use any Australian artist’s work without full permission,” John said.

John hosted the first Aria awards in 1987. The campaign wants AI companies to ask permission from and pay Australian artists before training on their work.

Its backers include music, film, TV and publishing groups, plus media firms such as News Corp, Foxtel and Seven. Guardian Australia, which reported the speech, is also a backer.

The campaign warns that changes sought by AI firms could put a $70bn creative industry and its 600,000 workers at risk, according to the Guardian. Aria put the campaign’s slogan on a billboard outside the venue.

Several winners also used their speeches to criticise AI, including Tim Minchin and Laneway festival co-founder Danny Rogers.

“If AI companies want to train on Australian music, it’s simple: pay us,” musician Ben Lee told Guardian Australia.

The government ruled out a text and data mining exception for AI in October 2025. But creative groups fear it could revisit copyright as it courts AI investment, after leaked slides showed it weighing an opt-out model.

Anthropic has proposed such a model, under which AI firms could train on works unless rights holders objected, the Guardian reported. A spokesperson for Attorney-General Michelle Rowland told the paper that any changes would give creators control and fair pay.

The government is expected to unveil a package of AI laws, including on copyright, in late 2026 or early 2027.
